title: Lambani patchwork embroidery
summary: Lambani embroidery is made by Banjara women of Karnataka and neighbouring states in India. Strips of cloth in red, yellow, teal and dark blue are patched together, covered with dense bands of herringbone and ladder stitch, and trimmed with cowrie shells and tiny mirrors.
howToPlay: Choose a thread colour and a stitch shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the patchwork to stitch it; its mirror partners are stitched too.
Copy the plan beside the cloth, then press Check.
rules: The design mirrors left to right and top to bottom, so each shape you stitch is also worked on its partner squares.
The round white shape is the cowrie shell.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the plan; undo and clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Lambani embroidery belongs to the Banjara communities, who once travelled with trade caravans and now live in settled villages. Women stitch their own skirts, bags and wall cloths, and their patchwork has become well known beyond the region.
